claims.statement: create_chess_agent wraps every user middleware with guard(), orders the stack as ChessCore, then ForcedMoveMiddleware (when forced_move), then the guarded extensions, then ChessSummarization for memory='summarize' or a NoSummarization placeholder when fixed_topology=True, and builds the agent with create_agent(tools=[]), substituting a NoModel that raises when model is None.
The write guard exists to make mistakes in trusted in-process middleware fail loudly with ChessContractError; it is explicitly not a security boundary.
guard() refuses middleware that registers tools and refuses an overridden async node hook that is not a coroutine function, raising ChessContractError.

create_chess_agent fails construction if two extensions declare the same own state key, or if the compiled input schema exposes keys beyond messages and position (unmarked extension keys or redeclared ChessState keys).

The guard proxy defines a hook only where the inner middleware's class overrides AgentMiddleware, preserving the inner name, state_schema, trace_policy, transformers and can_jump_to metadata, because create_agent detects hooks by identity and builds sync and async nodes separately.
Guarded hooks receive a detached state in which every ChessState key is deep-copied (own keys pass through), so in-place mutation of state has no effect on the graph.

Node-hook updates must be None, a dict, or Command(update=dict); besides jump_to and the middleware's own schema keys, only allowed_moves, proposal, fallback_move and candidates may be written, and other ChessState keys are refused as core-owned.

The guard requires allowed_moves writes to be non-empty subsets of the current allowed moves, and validates proposal, fallback_move and candidates against the allowed set as narrowed within the same update.

Only one proposal may exist per turn: the guard refuses a proposal write when state already holds a proposal, requires a well-formed Proposal (uci and source strings, string analysis, JSON meta, no extra keys), and requires its uci to be an allowed move.

candidates must be a duplicate-free subset of allowed_moves and have a single writer per turn: the guard records the writer in candidates_by and refuses a different middleware, while the same writer may rewrite them.

Candidates are soft: the prompt shows only candidates still in allowed_moves and tells the model it may play any allowed move, and ForcedMoveMiddleware reads initial_allowed rather than candidates or allowed_moves.

A command returned from a guarded wrap_model_call via ExtendedModelResponse may write only the middleware's own keys; it is checked inside the proxy because create_agent strips inner ExtendedModelResponses.

ChessMiddleware.propose returns a proposal (source defaulting to the middleware name) with jump_to end, narrow keeps only currently allowed moves in current order, and position returns a PositionView with allowed, initial_allowed, candidates, turn_id and a board() replayed from the root.

A proposer must declare @hook_config(can_jump_to=['end']) or its jump is silently ignored, and a turn that jumps to end with neither a proposal nor an outcome fails at commit with a ChessContractError.
At commit ChessCore re-checks that the proposal is legal and in allowed_moves, so narrowing after a proposal causes a ChessContractError; a non-LLM proposal's meta.model becomes Ply.model.

ChessCore stores each extension's non-None ply_meta under Ply.meta[name] when a move commits, and folds every extension's turn_calls into TurnRecord.calls and turn_latency_ms into TurnRecord.latency_ms once when a turn commits, terminates, or is abandoned; the proxy passes detached state to all three.

ChessCore resets proposal, terminal_intent, candidates, candidates_by, fallback_move and failed_call when a turn opens, retries from scratch or finalizes, but never clears extension-owned keys; a cross-run retry also restores allowed_moves to initial_allowed unless a validated proposal or terminal intent exists.

An in-run retry after an illegal reply jumps back to the model and re-enters before_model without resetting allowed_moves or candidates, so before_model must be idempotent; the illegal-reply budget is counted on TurnRecord.illegal_attempts rather than in reset state.
fallback_move must be an allowed move; core only resets it, and the UCI adapter plays it after a cancelled or failed search when it belongs to the same request and is in the root move pool.

SystemOneMiddleware freezes its decision in the private key systemone_turn keyed by turn_id, ranks only when no decision matches the current turn, and on every later before_model replays it instead of re-ranking.

SystemOneMiddleware._replay writes only what is still allowed: fallback_move if still allowed, a systemone proposal if the played move is still allowed, or candidates filtered to allowed moves; a skipped decision replays as nothing.
SystemOne derives its ranking seed from agent_seed and turn_id via SHA-256, and guard() copies create_chess_agent's seed onto ChessMiddleware.agent_seed.
guard() refuses a ChessMiddleware instance already bound to a different seed by an earlier agent, so an instance may be shared only by agents with the same seed.

When a model call fails after some provider calls completed, ChessCore.wrap_model_call keeps those calls and sets failed_call, after_model hooks run with no new reply, ChessCore.after_model re-raises the original error in that run, and on a later resume it clears failed_call and jumps back to the model.
SystemOneMiddleware reports its frozen decision's latency through turn_latency_ms, so ranking time is counted once per turn across retries.

The server passes a SystemOne middleware (or NoSystemOne) and GameSetupMiddleware to create_chess_agent with fixed_topology=True; GameSetupMiddleware declares an OmitFromInput but non-private setup key that it writes only on the run that opened the game's first turn, from both before_agent and after_agent.
